ROUTE_IDENTITY.detail: The route key obligation:track-pathway:IL:il-seal-3yr:adult-conviction-sealing is identical in the MASTER_QUEUE.json family row and in production-field-map.json. The paper carries the route and the fixtures carry different limbs of it deliberately: Request item 12 ticked Yes on packet page 4 in both fixtures; on page 5 the canonical fixture ticks Section 19.c, 'I completed an Illinois prison or jail sentence AND 3 years have passed since the end of my last sentence', and the boundary fixture ticks Section 19.b, 'My sentence of conditional discharge or probation was revoked AND 3 years have passed since the end of my last sentence'. Both are three-year sealing limbs, so both fixtures are on this route, and neither ticks 19.a, which is the two-year limb belonging to il-seal-2yr-set. The sealing table's Outcome cell carries FC, the form's own printed sealing abbreviation for a felony conviction, and the expungement table on Request page 2 is wholly blank. This matches what FIX118 recorded, and I read it off the pages rather than off its report.

KNOWN_PREFILLS.detail: All 44 declared writes produce readable ink. Of the 43 that carry drawn text, 42 match exactly against the extracted reading-order text of the packet page their document and page map to, and the one exception is the Section 19.c check box, whose stored value is the string 'Yes' and whose ink is the tick I located on page 5 by its printed context. No ellipsized value survives: I searched both whole fixtures for an ellipsis character and found none.

REQUIRED_BEFORE_FILING.detail: All ten of the record's requiredBeforeFiling lines are present verbatim in participant-instructions.md by exact string containment, and all 58 blanks the field map classes requiredBeforeFiling are named in the guide. The election-column defect VF05 scored here is repaired, and I verified the repair's factual claims rather than accepting them. The guide now states that the record places the per-case election in a Case List per-case election column, that the official Case List ships with no such column, and that 'its 78 form fields are the county, five caption fields, one clerk-assigned case number, one More Arrests or Case Numbers box and seventy unlabelled arrest or case cells, and not one of them is an election field'. I enumerated the widgets of the bound Case List binary myself: exactly 78, of which 70 are named arrest1 through arrest70 and the other 8 are '1 - County', '2 - Your name', '3 - Other name', '4 - Date of birth', '5 - Race', '6 - Gender', '7 - Case Number' and 'Page 1 - More Arrests or Case Numbers'. The claim is exactly right. The guide then says the election was made on the Request instead, at item 12 and the Section 19 limb, and tells the participant to correct it on the Request rather than the Case List - which is where the packet actually made it. This is the wording il-exp-qualprob-set and il-seal-2yr-set still lack. grep -c 'Complete arrest' on the delivered guide is 0, where VF05 found eleven such lines.

ROUTE_OPTIONS.detail: No refusal in the family carries routeDetermined true, and every election the route determines is ticked: Request item 12 Yes, the Section 19 limb (19.c canonical, 19.b boundary), the self-represented box on Request page 6 and the self-represented box on FW-CIV page 4. Each tick is the form's own ZapfDingbats mark drawn inside the form's own printed empty-box glyph rather than pdf-lib's synthesized check inside a synthesized hairline square. The guide gives the Section 19 election a section of its own that explains what a reader could not otherwise know - that Section 19 has no box of its own, so ticking a limb is how the statement is made - names which limb this packet ticked, tells the participant to untick it and tick the other if the certified record shows the other, and warns against ticking both and against ticking 19.a because that is the two-year limb and a different route. Nothing on the proposed Order is ticked, which the form itself directs.

FILING_DESTINATION.detail: The registry's destination is {kind: clerk, name: 'Circuit clerk of the county of arrest or charge', detail: 'File with the circuit clerk in each county where an arrest occurred or a charge was brought. The clerk performs service under section 5.2(d)(4).'}. The guide carries it under 'Where this is filed', naming what to file together (Request, Case List, any Additional Cases forms and the proposed Order), the county-by-county rule, and the AOIC flattening requirement for e-filing, and repeats the county rule and the Cook County district rule in the service section.

FEE_AND_WAIVER.detail: Both are stated in the record's own words under 'What it costs, and the waiver': a circuit clerk fee plus an ISP processing fee, both county-collected, ISP charging nothing to file a petition and $60 to process a court order, county totals commonly roughly $60 to $235 with McLean County publishing $136, and the instruction to treat every figure as county-specific. The waiver is shipped, not merely named: the Supreme Court Rule 298 Application for Waiver of Court Fees is component 4, rendered as packet pages 10-13, and the guide states that section 5.2(d)(1) requires no fee where a Rule 298 order has been obtained or the fee is otherwise waived. The guide also states that the packet makes none of the waiver form's financial statements and lists all 46 of its check boxes as the participant's, which is the defect VF05 raised and FIX118 repaired in its second round.

SERVICE.detail: '## Who serves, and how' names the method - 'The circuit court clerk serves, under section 5.2(d)(4). The participant serves no one.' - and the recipients - the State's Attorney, the Illinois State Police, the arresting agency, and for municipal ordinance violations the chief legal officer - with the 60-day objection period under section 5.2(d)(5)(B) and the rule that absent an objection the court shall enter an order granting or denying under section 5.2(d)(6)(B). It adds that a separate flattened packet is filed with the clerk in each county, that Cook County filings go to the district matching the case, that a hearing date is added only when the clerk or court supplies it, and that court-owned service and order fields are not to be completed. I confirmed from the bytes that no service or certificate-of-service field is written.

SELF_HELP_STOP.detail: The registry track names eight selfHelpStopConditions and all eight are printed verbatim under '## Stop and get help', confirmed one by one by exact string containment: an objection by the State's Attorney, ISP, the arresting agency or the chief legal officer; a contested hearing; an ambiguous or contested disposition on the transcript; an unrecognised case on the transcript which may indicate identity theft; federal or out-of-state records an Illinois court cannot reach; immigration consequences; a motion to vacate, modify or reconsider under section 5.2(d)(12); and denial of the petition. VF05's specific objection is discharged too: the loose paraphrase 'the printed eligibility facts do not match', which stood where the record says 'The disposition on the transcript is ambiguous or contested', is gone with the single sentence that carried it.
